deviations.what: the sap.m.plugins.UploadSetwithTable control (since UI5 1.124) is newer than 1.71 and is the whole point of this sample - kept 1:1 in the table's dependents as plugins:UploadSetwithTable (the original's dotted plugins.UploadSetwithTable under the sap.m default namespace), with its rowConfiguration aggregation; the app needs a UI5 release >= 1.124. Every member it carries (uploadUrl, multiple, cloudFilePickerEnabled, the actions association, beforeUploadStarts, itemRenamed, uploadCompleted) is as new as the plugin.

the plugin's companion controls are kept 1:1 and are post-1.71 too: sap.m.upload.ActionsPlaceholder (@since 1.120, with placeholderFor - the toolbar slot the plugin renders its upload button into) and sap.m.upload.UploadItemConfiguration (@since 1.124; fileNamePath, mediaTypePath, urlPath, previewablePath and fileSizePath @1.124, isTrustedSourcePath @1.125), written upload:UploadItemConfiguration for the original's dotted upload.UploadItemConfiguration.

sap.m.Column importance (@since 1.76) on the File Name and action columns, and sap.m.Table autoPopinMode (@since 1.76) and hiddenInPopin (@since 1.77), are kept 1:1 from the original table, as is its growing='true'.

The named JSONModel documents (manifest dataSource model/documents.json) is folded into the default model: every {documents>x} binding is the row field {X} and the items path is the bound T_ITEMS, still as the original's {path, templateShareable: false} binding info. All nine rows are inlined; the url and imageUrl fields are host-absolutized to https://sdk.openui5.org/test-resources/... because an abap2UI5 app has no demo-kit root to resolve the relative test-resources paths against. The UploadItemConfiguration paths name the upper-case ABAP fields (FILENAME, MEDIATYPE, URL, PREVIEWABLE, FILESIZE, TRUSTEDSOURCE) instead of fileName/mediaType/... - the same model columns. IMAGEURL and UPLOADSTATE are bound with omit_initial_paths, so a row the mock gives no imageUrl/uploadState still reads undefined and the original's own Image/Icon visible expressions and highlight expression decide exactly as in the sample.

The controller formatters getIconSrc (UploadSetwithTable.getIconForFileType - IconPool's media-type table, the file-extension fallback with sap-icon://card for images) and getFileSizeWithUnits (KB/MB/GB with two decimals) run in ABAP (icon_for, size_with_units) and the row carries the finished values in two port fields, ICON and FILESIZE_UNITS, which core:Icon.src and the File Size Text bind - the thin-frontend rule; the {parts: [...], formatter: ...} bindings are gone with them.

Upload progress - the point of this variant - is not reproduced. The controller's onBeforeUploadStarts builds a ColumnListItem in JS (a Text with the file name, a VBox with a ProgressIndicator 'Uploading..' label, a stop Button wired to terminateUpload, four empty Controls and a decline Button), inserts it with oTable.insertItem and drives it from the item's uploadProgress / uploadTerminated events; none of these controls exist in the view and their handlers are JS closures over live UploadItem instances, so beforeUploadStarts is not wired at all and no progress row appears. The upload itself goes out as in the original (the sample switches its mock server OFF here, so the POST to /uploadFiles reaches whatever server hosts the app and does not answer 201). onUploadCompleted is a backend wire: it transports the item's file name, url, getFileSize( ) and the response status, and the backend unshifts the row the controller builds - id 'id' plus a running number where the controller appends new Date().getTime(), no media type because the controller stores it under fileType (which no binding reads), uploadState Complete - and shows 'Document Added' only for a status of 201, like the controller (without its one-second setTimeout). The progress rows' bookkeeping (aProgressItems) and URLListValidator.add('blob') are dropped. Several files picked at once complete back to back while abap2UI5 runs one round-trip at a time: check_queue_last keeps the last one, so only the first and the last of them are added. onActivated is not wired; the plugin is addressed by an added id uploadSetPlugin instead of the instance onActivated handed the controller.

onDownloadFiles calls the plugin's download( context, true ) for EVERY selected row; a UI5 event expression has no loop, so the port's Download button calls download for the first selected row only, through a view-wired control_by_id on the plugin whose argument is $controller.getView().byId('table-uploadSet').getSelectedContexts()[0].

Unverified in a running system: (a) the plugin calls by id (uploadSetPlugin, an id the original does not carry) through the unlisted-method path of control_by_id - openFilePreview with the Link's $event.oSource.getBindingContext(), renameItem and download with $controller.getView().byId('table-uploadSet').getSelectedContexts()[0] - each handing the live Context object through castArgAuto untouched; (b) selectionChange transporting $event.oSource.getSelectedContexts().join() (Context.toString is the binding path) and the itemRenamed wire reading ${$parameters>/item}.getBindingContext().getPath(); (c) the uploadCompleted wire with ${$parameters>/item}.getFileSize() and ${$parameters>/status}.

onSelectionChange's setEnabled calls become two bound flags: Download is enabled for one or more selected rows, Remove/Rename/Edit URL for exactly one. onSearch's Filter('fileName', Contains, query) is the view-wired binding_call filter on the table's items with ${$source>/value} - roundtrip-free, and like any binding filter it does not survive a view rebuild. onDocumentRenamedSuccess writes the new name into the row in the backend (the itemRenamed wire carries the row's path and the item's file name) and toasts 'Document Renamed.' with duration 2000. After a removal the port resets the selection AND the four buttons; the original's removeSelections( ) fires no selectionChange, so there the buttons stayed enabled on an empty selection.

The AddViaUrl fragment is the port's popup with its ids kept (addViaUrlDialog, addViaUrlSimpleform, urlInputLabel, urlInput, nameInputLabel, nameInput, addDocumentBtn), and what openAddOrEditDialog / _isValidName / _validateAddOrEditUrlDialog set through Element.getElementById is bound instead: the Dialog title (Add URL / Edit URL), the begin button text (Add / Apply), urlInputLabel.required, both Input values and their valueState / valueStateText. Cancel closes it with popup_close. Add validates name and URL in the backend (the unanchored URL regex reduced to its required part, a ftp/http/https scheme followed by a non-blank) and then adds the row directly - uploadItemViaUrl takes a JS Promise and the controller adds a documentUrl header field to the item, neither transportable; with the mock server off, the empty file's upload completes without a 201, so onUploadCompleted adds the row (the URL as typed, size 0) and shows no toast, which is what the port does. showEditConfirmation's controller-built sap.m.Dialog (type Message, state Warning, title Warning, Save / DiscardChanges) is a MessageBox.warning with the same title, text, actions and Save emphasized; Save updates the selected row's fileName and url and closes the fragment, DiscardChanges only closes the box. removeItem's MessageBox.warning keeps its text, actions Remove/CANCEL, emphasizedAction, styleClass and initialFocus; its explicit icon option is the warning box's own icon anyway.
